title: Karl Organizing: Bust Cards
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Bust Cards] What should I have on me in case things go south?

Carry a 'bust card' with the local legal collective's phone number and a summary of your rights. Memorize that number too, because the pigs might take your card when they take your bag. Having that info ready turns a scary arrest into a manageable hurdle for the movement.

title: Karl Organizing: Labor Endorsements
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Labor Endorsements] Can you explain: how do I get unions to back a radical campaign?

Look, Show up on their picket lines long before you ask for their vote. Talk to the rank-and-file workers, not just the leadership, and prove you understand their specific grievances. Be the candidate who explicitly supports the right to strike and the expansion of collective bargaining. If you want the muscle of organized labor behind you, you have to be the most reliable ally they’ve ever seen in public office.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, donor Capture
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, donor Capture] A wealthy businessman wants to give us a large sum but has some 'suggestions' on our messaging. Should we take it?

Tell him to keep his blood money and his opinions. The second you let a fat cat dictate your slogans is the second you stop being a threat to his class. If he wants to help, he can drop the cash in the bucket and walk away with no strings attached; otherwise, he's just buying a leash to put on your movement.

title: Karl Organizing: Financial Transparency
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Financial Transparency] How do we handle the money we raise together?

Put one person from each major group in charge of a joint bank account and publish every single expense to the whole coalition. Nothing kills a movement faster than rumors about where the cash went, so be obsessed with being open. Use the funds to print flyers, pay for bail, and chip in for the gas it takes to get comrades to the front lines. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Safety in Numbers
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Safety in Numbers] The manager keeps cornering me in the hall to talk about my 'attitude.' Help?

Here's how it works: Never talk to management alone again. From now on, tell them any conversation about your tenancy must happen in writing or with a union witness present. If they corner you, pull out your phone, start recording, and walk away. When they realize they can't isolate and bully you, they'll stop trying and start fearing the collective instead.

title: Karl Organizing: Sustaining the Fight
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Sustaining the Fight] Can you explain: how do we keep people from burning out on rapid response?

Rotate your shifts and make sure nobody is on call 24/7 or they'll be useless within a month. Celebrate your wins, no matter how small, and make time for communal meals and joy that have nothing to do with the pigs. This is a marathon, not a sprint, and we need every comrade healthy and sharp for the long haul. Rest is a radical act when the state wants you exhausted. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: skill-sharing for Cash
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: skill-sharing for Cash] Give me the short version: How can we raise money using our own talents?

Here's the thing: Turn your movement into a school for the working class. Have your tech-savvy comrades run a workshop on digital security or your gardeners teach urban farming for a suggested sliding-scale fee. You're building the community's capacity and filling the treasury at the same time, which is a hell of a lot better than selling overpriced cookies.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, location Services
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, location Services] Should I keep my GPS on so my friends can find me in a crowd?

Turn that tracker off immediately. Every time your GPS pings, a billionaire’s server logs your exact coordinates, and the cops can buy that data with a simple request. Use a specific meeting point and a physical map instead. If you must use a map app, use Organic Maps or something that works offline. Don't let the enemy map your movements in real-time. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Ethical Banking
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Ethical Banking] A friend asked me: 'Where should we keep the movement's cash so it's safe?' What do I tell them?

Get your money out of the big Wall Street banks that fund pipelines and private prisons yesterday. Move the war chest to a local credit union or a community-owned bank where the staff actually knows your name. It won't solve capitalism, but at least your deposits aren't being used as a weapon against your own comrades while you sleep.

title: Karl Organizing: Legal Rights Training
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Legal Rights Training] A friend asked me: 'What's the most important thing to teach neighbors about their rights?' What do I tell them?

Here's how it works: The most powerful words anyone can say are 'I am remaining silent and I want a lawyer.' Teach everyone that the police are allowed to lie to you, so you should never believe a word they say during an interrogation. Run 'Know Your Rights' workshops in living rooms and parks until every kid on the block knows how to handle a stop. Knowledge is the first line of defense against the precinct.

title: Karl Organizing: The First Meeting
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[The First Meeting] A friend asked me: 'What is the most important thing to do at our very first coalition meeting?' What do I tell them?

Set a specific goal and a hard deadline for the first action before anyone leaves the room. Don't spend two hours introducing yourselves and sharing 'vibes'; identify the common enemy and decide on a date to make them sweat. A coalition that doesn't act immediately is just a book club with better slogans, and we are here to win, not study. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Street Medics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Street Medics] What basic supplies should we have for community defense?

Here's how it works: Every defense team needs a dedicated medic with a kit containing gauze, saline, gloves, and antacids for pepper spray. Don't just buy gear; get trained on how to use it so you aren't a liability when things go sideways. Keep your kit organized and your head on a swivel. We take care of our own because the system would rather see us bleed out on the sidewalk.

title: Karl Organizing: Free Clinic Logistics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Free Clinic Logistics] Can you explain: i want to start a free clinic, but none of us are doctors. Is it still possible?

Real talk: You don't need a medical degree to run a first-aid station or a herbal medicine collective, so start where you are. Focus on preventative care, wound cleaning, and distributing naloxone to keep our people alive in the streets. Partner with sympathetic nurses or EMTs who are tired of the insurance industry's greed and want to actually help folks. We're building a parallel system of care because the private hospitals would rather see us die than see us broke.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, conflict Resolution
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, conflict Resolution] Two people in our collective are fighting and it's stalling our work. What now?

Let me break it down: Sit them down with a neutral mediator and remind them that our real enemy is the ruling class, not each other. Focus on the harm caused and how to make it right rather than looking for someone to blame or 'cancel.' If we can't solve problems within our own ranks, we'll never be able to build a world that works for everyone. Keep the focus on the mission: feeding and protecting our people.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, vPN Usage
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, vPN Usage] Do I really need a VPN?

Look, A good VPN like Mullvad hides your traffic from your ISP, which is vital because ISPs are snitches by default. It won't make you invisible to the sites you visit, but it stops the company you pay for internet from building a dossier on your activism. It's a basic layer of defense. Pool resources with your crew to cover the costs of a solid, no-logs provider.

title: Karl Organizing: Skillshare Organization
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Skillshare Organization] Can you explain: i want to teach people how to fix bikes, but I've never organized a workshop before.

Look, Grab your tools, find a public park or a community center, and put up some flyers with a clear time and date. Keep it hands-on and skip the long lectures—people learn best by doing, not by listening to us talk. Make sure the space is accessible to everyone and encourage those who learn quickly to start helping the newcomers. We're breaking the monopoly on knowledge that the bosses use to keep us dependent and helpless.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, district Attorney races
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, district Attorney races] How does a radical DA change anything without changing the law?

The law is a weapon, and the DA chooses where to point it. You stop prosecuting low-level drug offenses, refuse to seek the death penalty, and go after wage theft and corporate polluters instead of the poor. It’s about taking the boot off the necks of our people by exercising the power of non-prosecution. Turn that office into a consumer protection agency for the working class and a nightmare for the exploitative bosses.

title: Karl Organizing: Filming Police
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Filming Police] Can you explain: is it legal for me to record the police while they are making arrests?

It is your right to film the police in public, so keep those cameras rolling and don't let them intimidate you into stopping. Stay a few feet back so they can't claim you're interfering, and try to live-stream so the evidence is safe even if they smash your gear. Documenting their brutality is the only way we hold these goons accountable in the court of public opinion.

title: Karl Organizing: Digital Security
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Digital Security] How do I keep my phone safe from the police at a rally?

Look, Karl's answer: Turn off FaceID and TouchID before you even get to the rally, as the cops can force those open but they can't force your brain to give up a passcode. Switch your phone to airplane mode or use a Faraday bag to prevent location tracking. If you're doing real work, leave the personal phone at home and use a burner or an encrypted tablet.

title: Karl Organizing: The Sheriff's Office
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[The Sheriff's Office] Is it worth running for Sheriff to abolish the position?

Running for Sheriff is about immediate harm reduction and throwing a wrench in the deportation machine. You can refuse to cooperate with ICE, stop the eviction crews from throwing families on the street, and end the barbaric practice of cash bail in your county. We want the office gone, but until it is, we need a comrade holding the keys who refuses to turn them against the working class. Use the power to de-escalate, demilitarize, and defend the vulnerable. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Small Group Value
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Small Group Value] Can you explain: is it worth the time joining up with tiny local groups that only have five members?

A hundred pebbles make a landslide if you throw them at the same time. Those tiny groups have deep roots in their specific neighborhoods that your big city organization will never have. Respect their local knowledge, share your printing press and bullhorns, and build a front that the bosses can't ignore just by looking at a map.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: de-escalation
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: de-escalation] Give me the short version: How can we handle a neighborhood dispute without calling the cops?

Cops only bring guns to a conversation, so we handle our own business by sending a small team of neutral neighbors to listen to both sides. Focus on the harm done and how to fix it rather than who broke what rule. If things get heated, separate the parties and let tempers cool before trying to find a resolution. We build safety through relationships and accountability, not through handcuffs and cages. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: street Medics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: street Medics] Give me the short version: What basic supplies should we have for community defense?

Let me break it down: Every defense team needs a dedicated medic with a kit containing gauze, saline, gloves, and antacids for pepper spray. Don't just buy gear; get trained on how to use it so you aren't a liability when things go sideways. Keep your kit organized and your head on a swivel. We take care of our own because the system would rather see us bleed out on the sidewalk.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: mental Health Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: mental Health Support] Give me the short version: A comrade is having a crisis. How do we help without calling the police?

Real talk: Show up with a small team of calm, trusted friends and stay with them until the storm passes. Listen more than you speak and help them navigate their immediate needs, like food or a safe place to sleep. We've seen too many of our people killed by 'wellness checks,' so we take care of our own minds and hearts. Build a network of peer-support volunteers who are trained in de-escalation and crisis intervention.

title: Karl Organizing: Two-Factor Authentication
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Two-Factor Authentication] Is using my phone number for 2FA safe?

It’s a trap. SIM swapping is a common tactic where someone convinces your carrier to move your number to their phone, giving them access to all your accounts. Use an authentication app like Aegis or a physical security key like a YubiKey instead. Never use your phone number as a security layer if you can avoid it; it's the weakest link in the chain.

title: Karl Organizing: New Neighbor Outreach
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[New Neighbor Outreach] A new family just moved in. How do we bring them into the union?

Don't wait for them to have a problem; go over with a housewarming gift and the union's contact info on day one. Explain that the building stays safe and the rent stays stable only because you all look out for each other. Getting them on board early prevents the landlord from using them as a 'scab' to undermine the collective power you've built. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Intervention Ethics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Intervention Ethics] A friend asked me: 'When should I actually step in if I see a cop harassing someone?' What do I tell them?

Here's how it works: Assess the situation and ask the person being harassed if they want help before you dive in. If they say yes, start filming and ask the officer for their name and badge number while standing at a safe distance. Sometimes just having three or four people watching silently with phones out is enough to make a bully in uniform back off. Solidarity means following the lead of the person in the crosshairs.

title: Karl Organizing: Mental Health Crisis
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Mental Health Crisis] Can you explain: what do we do if a neighbor is having a mental health breakdown?

Look, Calling 911 is a death sentence for people in crisis, so you need a team of neighbors trained in psychological first aid. Approach with empty hands, keep your voice low, and give the person plenty of physical space. Find out if they have a friend or a therapist they trust and get that person on the scene. Our goal is to bring them back to earth safely, not to restrain or terrorize them.

title: Karl Organizing: Mental Health Crisis
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, digital Security
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, digital Security] Is it safe to use Facebook to organize our bail fund and protests?

Here's the thing: Delete those apps and get your crew onto Signal or another encrypted platform immediately. The tech giants are happy to hand your data over to the feds the second things get spicy. Keep your sensitive talk off the grid and save the social media for public announcements and recruitment only. We don't give the state a roadmap to our resistance just because a platform is convenient to use.

title: Karl Organizing: Resource Sharing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Resource Sharing] Can you explain: how do we handle money and tools between different groups?

Create a shared pool of resources where the groups with more cash chip in to help the groups with more people. Total transparency is the only way this works, so keep a public ledger that every member can see. Share the bullhorns, the high-speed printers, and the mailing lists like they belong to the movement, because the bosses already own everything else. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Crowd Logistics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Crowd Logistics] Can you explain: how do we stay organized when things get chaotic in the street?

Use the 'buddy system' so nobody is ever standing alone or getting snatched without a witness. Assign roles like 'scout,' 'vibe checker,' and 'legal' so everyone knows exactly what their job is when the pressure starts. If the group needs to move, do it together in a tight block rather than scattering. A disorganized crowd is a target; an organized community is a force.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, rotating Roles
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, rotating Roles] Should the same person always be the spokesperson for the coalition?

Absolutely not, because that creates a bottleneck and a target for the bosses to bribe or smear. Train as many comrades as possible to speak to the press and lead the meetings so the movement doesn't collapse if one person gets sick or arrested. A leaderless movement is hard to stop, but a leader-full movement where everyone is capable is invincible. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Secret organizing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Secret organizing] Why do we have to keep our union talk a secret at first?

Loose lips get comrades fired. If the boss finds out you're organizing before you have a solid core of supporters, they'll pick you off one by one for 'performance issues' or some other lie. You keep it underground to build your strength in the shadows. Once you've got the numbers, you come out as a united front that's too big to crush.

title: Karl Organizing: Code Enforcement
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Code Enforcement] The city inspector never does anything. How do we get them to actually fine the landlord?

One call is a nuisance; thirty calls in one morning is a crisis. Coordinate your union to flood the code enforcement line all at once so the city can't ignore the volume. When the inspector shows up, have a committee of tenants ready to walk them through every unit to point out the rot they usually 'miss.' Don't let them leave until they've written a citation for every single violation they saw.

title: Karl Organizing: Dealing with Small Landlords
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Dealing with Small Landlords] My landlord is just a 'mom and pop' who says they're struggling too. Should I be nicer?

Real talk: The 'mom and pop' label is a mask for the same exploitative relationship. If they're struggling, they can sell the building to the tenants; they shouldn't be balance-billing their life on your back. A small-scale parasite still lives off your paycheck while you deal with the broken boiler. Treat them like a business because that's exactly how they'll treat you when the rent is late.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, harm Reduction
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, harm Reduction] People are using drugs near our community fridge. How do we handle this safely?

Stop judging and start helping; hand out clean needles and Narcan instead of calling the cops who will only make it worse. Train your fridge volunteers on how to spot an overdose and how to use a reversal kit without hesitating. We treat our neighbors with dignity, especially those the system has discarded and left to struggle with addiction. Safety comes from community care and presence, not from displacement and state violence.

title: Karl Organizing: Avoiding Burnout
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Avoiding Burnout] A friend asked me: 'I'm the candidate and I'm exhausted. How do I keep going?' What do I tell them?

You have to trust your comrades. You aren't a lone hero; you are a representative of a collective movement. Delegate the logistics and the admin work so you can focus on the one thing only you can do: looking your neighbors in the eye and giving them hope. Take a night off to eat a real meal and sleep, because a candidate who collapses from exhaustion is no use to the revolution.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: signature Gathering
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: signature Gathering] Give me the short version: How do we get on the ballot without a massive paid staff?

You need a brigade of volunteers who believe in the cause enough to hit the pavement every single weekend. Set up at grocery stores, transit hubs, and public parks to meet people where they already are. Treat every signature as a conversation and a potential new recruit for the movement, not just a box to check. We don't need consultants when we have a disciplined crew of comrades who know how to ask a neighbor for two minutes of their time.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, member Dues
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, member Dues] How do we get people to pay dues every month?

Stop treating it like a Netflix subscription and start treating it like war insurance. Tell your comrades clearly: we don't take a dime from the bosses, which means the lights only stay on if we keep the fuel coming ourselves. Set up a sliding scale so the barista chips in five and the union plumber chips in fifty; it keeps the power in our hands, not some billionaire's foundation. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Sliding Scales
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Sliding Scales] How do we implement a sliding scale for events?

Be explicit about who each tier is for. Label the low end for students and the unemployed, the middle for workers, and the high end for 'solidarity' from those with a little extra cushion. It forces people to reflect on their own class position and ensures that the struggle remains accessible to the very people we're fighting for. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Membership Perks
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Membership Perks] A friend asked me: 'Do we need to give donors gifts like tote bags or stickers?' What do I tell them?

The best 'perk' you can give a comrade is a victory against the bosses. Don't waste money on trinkets that eat into your margins. Give them a vote in the organization, a seat at the strategy table, and the knowledge that they are part of a serious force for change; that's worth more than any canvas bag.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, location Services
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, location Services] Should I keep my GPS on so my friends can find me in a crowd?

Turn that tracker off immediately. Every time your GPS pings, a billionaire’s server logs your exact coordinates, and the cops can buy that data with a simple request. Use a specific meeting point and a physical map instead. If you must use a map app, use Organic Maps or something that works offline. Don't let the enemy map your movements in real-time.

title: Karl Organizing: Local Business Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Local Business Support] A friend asked me: 'Is it okay to ask the coffee shop down the street for a donation?' What do I tell them?

If it's a true local shop and not a franchise, go for it. These small business owners are often getting squeezed by the same banks and landlords we're fighting. Ask them to put out a jar or host a 'community day' where a percentage of sales goes to the movement; it builds a bridge between the organizers and the neighborhood.

title: Karl Organizing: Accountability
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Accountability] A friend asked me: 'What if one group isn't doing the work they promised to do?' What do I tell them?

Have a direct, face-to-face conversation and ask them what the bottleneck is. If they are overwhelmed, offer help; if they are just being lazy or posturing, tell them they are holding back the whole movement. We don't have time for passengers when we're trying to sink the billionaire's ship, so everyone has to pull their weight or get out of the way. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Legal observers
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Legal observers] What do legal observers do?

They watch the police, not the protesters. Green hats, notebooks, cameras. They document badge numbers, times, and exactly what officers do — because courts believe contemporaneous notes. Contact the National Lawyers Guild to get trained. Legal observers don't participate; they witness. That neutrality is their power.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, building a Platform
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, building a Platform] What should be at the top of my local campaign platform?

Housing as a human right, period. If you aren't talking about rent control, social housing, and an end to homelessness, you aren't serious about helping the working class. Add in a demand for robust public transit and a promise to tax the big local businesses to pay for it all. Keep the language simple and the promises bold so the average person knows exactly whose side you are on from the jump.

title: Karl Organizing: Dealing with a hostile landlord
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Dealing with a hostile landlord] My landlord is retaliating against me. What now?

Document everything — dates, times, photos, witnesses. Retaliation is illegal in most states, but only if you can prove the timeline. Send all communications in writing. Contact a tenant lawyer or legal aid immediately. And tell your neighbors — retaliation thrives on isolation, and a landlord who retaliates against one tenant will do it to others. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, encrypted Messaging
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, encrypted Messaging] Why should I bother with Signal when I have nothing to hide?

Privacy isn't about having secrets; it's about power. When you use unencrypted SMS, you're handing a transcript of your life to the state and the billionaire carriers. Use Signal for everything. Set your messages to disappear after five minutes so there's no paper trail for some ambitious prosecutor to use against your crew. We protect our own by leaving no tracks. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: surveillance Awareness
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: surveillance Awareness] Give me the short version: What is a Stingray and should I be worried about it?

Here's the thing: A Stingray is a fake cell tower the feds use to hijack your phone's signal and track your location. They use them to map out who is at a protest and who they're talking to. Put your phone in a Faraday bag or turn on Airplane Mode when you're near the action. If you don't need to coordinate in real-time, leave the tracking device at home.

title: Karl Organizing: Transparent Treasuries
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Transparent Treasuries] A friend asked me: 'How do we keep people from worrying about where the money goes?' What do I tell them?

Look, Radical transparency is the only way to build real trust. Post a simple, plain-English breakdown of every dollar spent on a public board or in your newsletter every single month. When people see that their hard-earned cash is buying flyers and bail buttons instead of fancy dinners for leaders, they'll be lining up to chip in again.

title: Karl Organizing: Internal Conflict
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Internal Conflict] A friend asked me: 'What do we do when two groups in the coalition start fighting each other?' What do I tell them?

Drag them back to the shared demand and remind them who the real enemy is. If the beef is personal, tell them to settle it on their own time because the warehouse workers or the tenants are waiting on us to lead. We aren't here to be a family; we are here to be a fist, and a fist doesn't work if the fingers are trying to snap each other.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: city Council motivation
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: city Council motivation] Give me the short version: Why should I run for city council when the real power is in DC?

The feds won't stop your landlord from hiking the rent, but a council vote can. We're seizing the levers that actually touch people’s lives every single morning—the cops, the zoning, and the water bills. Grab a clipboard, talk to the people at the bus stop, and let’s start making the bosses sweat where they actually live. Don't wait for a savior from the capital when you can be the shield for your own block right now.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, jail Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, jail Support] How do I make sure someone is waiting for me if I get arrested?

Look, Write the legal support number on your arm in permanent marker before you head out. Once you get your phone call, give them your name, your location, and what you're being charged with. Our people will be outside the jail with snacks, water, and a ride home the second you're released because we never leave a comrade behind.

title: Karl Organizing: Phone Hygiene
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Phone Hygiene] Can you explain: what's the best way to back up my phone before an action?

Back it up to a local hard drive at home, then encrypt that drive with a strong password. Turn off all auto-syncing to the cloud—Apple and Google will hand over your 'private' backups the moment the state asks. Once your backup is safe at home, wipe any sensitive messages or photos from the device you're carrying. Travel light and travel clean.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: grant Alternatives
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: grant Alternatives] Give me the short version: Foundation grants seem easier than grassroots fundraising. Why avoid them?

Real talk: Foundations are just tax shelters for the wealthy designed to domesticate the revolution. They'll bury you in paperwork and 'deliverables' until you're too busy writing reports to actually organize. We build our own solidarity funds through community dinners and sustainer circles so we never have to ask a board of directors for permission to speak the truth.

title: Karl Organizing: Skill-sharing for Cash
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Skill-sharing for Cash] A friend asked me: 'How can we raise money using our own talents?' What do I tell them?

Real talk: Turn your movement into a school for the working class. Have your tech-savvy comrades run a workshop on digital security or your gardeners teach urban farming for a suggested sliding-scale fee. You're building the community's capacity and filling the treasury at the same time, which is a hell of a lot better than selling overpriced cookies.

title: Karl Organizing: Internal Conflict
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Internal Conflict] A friend asked me: 'What do we do when two groups in the coalition start fighting each other?' What do I tell them?

Look, Drag them back to the shared demand and remind them who the real enemy is. If the beef is personal, tell them to settle it on their own time because the warehouse workers or the tenants are waiting on us to lead. We aren't here to be a family; we are here to be a fist, and a fist doesn't work if the fingers are trying to snap each other.

title: Karl Organizing: The 1-on-1 conversation
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[The 1-on-1 conversation] How do I talk to a coworker who is scared of the boss?

You don't lecture them; you listen. Ask them what's wrong with the job and let them find their own anger. Once they're talking about the low pay or the unsafe conditions, show them that the only person who can fix it is the person standing next to them. Agitate them, educate them, and then give them a plan to take that power back together. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: power Mapping
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: power Mapping] Give me the short version: How do we know which politician or CEO to target first?

Real talk: Map out who actually signs the checks or passes the laws, then find out who those people are actually afraid of. Don't just protest into the void; find the specific person—the landlord, the CEO, the Council Chair—who has the power to give you what you want right now. Once you find that pressure point, you squeeze together as a coalition until they crack under the weight.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, rotating Roles
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, rotating Roles] Should the same person always be the spokesperson for the coalition?

Look, Absolutely not, because that creates a bottleneck and a target for the bosses to bribe or smear. Train as many comrades as possible to speak to the press and lead the meetings so the movement doesn't collapse if one person gets sick or arrested. A leaderless movement is hard to stop, but a leader-full movement where everyone is capable is invincible.
